title: Constrained diffusion-enabled construction of a highly expressed and robust peptide asparaginyl ligase
summary: An AI-assisted enzyme-design study reported a peptide ligase with higher thermal stability and soluble expression than the natural comparators tested, while retaining catalytic activity. The results are specific to the studied enzyme and assay conditions.
ai_technology: A denoising diffusion model generates candidate peptide-ligase scaffolds; prediction tools guide candidate prioritization before experimental screening and refinement.
organization: China Pharmaceutical University; Institute of Microbiology, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Beijing University of Chemical Technology

evidence.tested: The tested enzyme showed reported melting temperature of 69 °C, soluble expression near 64 mg/L, and catalytic efficiency comparable to the cited natural comparator.
evidence.unknown: The result is specific to the tested enzyme and assays; broader application performance is not established. No sequence or experimental protocol is reproduced.
evidence.ai_role: Diffusion-based sequence generation and learned stability prioritization contributed to an experimentally tested ligase result.

source_review.scope: Primary source full-text Methods and Results; version date and reported validation scope checked.
